title: Operationalize Redwood-verified performance profiles with regional mirrors and cost-normalized metrics
creator: Ariana Chen
description:
Purpose: Make Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency, throughput, cost) first-class artifacts that are reproducible across regions, resilient to infrastructure variance, and explicitly cost-normalized so teams can safely pin model versions in production. This ticket scopes the publishing pipeline changes, the staging->mirror promotion flow, and the acceptance windows used to mark a profile as 'verified'.

Background: We already produce verification artifacts for models but teams report occasional region-to-region variance (different kernel sets / GPU types) and confusion about cost numbers that are not normalized for batch shape and tokenization. We also lack a deterministic, auditable staging-to-production promotion path that maintains compatibility with existing pinning/rollback workflows.

Goals:
- Define canonical normalization rules for cost (tokens/sec + instance type sensitivity) so cost fields are comparable across profiles.
- Add a regional mirror validation stage: publish profile to staging, run mirrored verification in 3 representative regions, and require pass/fail criteria before marking global-verified.
- Make verification artifacts self-describing and reproducible: include seed, workload definition, toolkit version, kernel subset hash, and execution environment tags.
- Expose a lightweight 'soft-pin' recommendation for customers: recommended model+profile pair with rollforward guidance if region mismatch is observed.

Out of scope: major UI console redesign and on-prem installation packaging changes (those will be separate follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: A cost-normalization algorithm is documented and checked into the perf-profile spec (includes tokenization normalization, batch-shape normalization, and instance-type multipliers).
Publishing pipeline writes self-describing verification artifacts (workload.json, env-tags.txt, kernel-hash.txt) alongside the profile manifest in the registry.
Staging->regional-mirror run completes automatically for a sample set of models and enforces a 3-region quorum for marking profile status 'global-verified'.
Profiles published via the new flow surface normalized cost in the API and Console and include provenance links (benchmark run IDs, PRs, and infra snapshots).
Documentation and a short runbook for oncall explaining how to interpret region variance and how to trigger a re-run are published.
steps: Design and agree on cost-normalization formula with Research/Applied ML (1 week).
Extend verification harness to emit reproducibility metadata (seed, model hash, tokenizer version, kernel set).
Implement mirror runner in the publishing pipeline to spin verification jobs in 3 target regions (us-west-2, eu-central-1, ap-southeast-1).
Create promotion policy that uses region pass ratio and outlier detection to mark profile as global-verified or regional-limited.
Update registry schema to store normalized_cost and provenance URLs; add required fields to the signed manifest.
Add Console rows and API fields for normalized_cost and verification provenance (follow-up small UI PR).
Write runbook and update model-onboarding checklist.
